brief: UBS's European morning note recaps Wednesday's US session and sets up Thursday's European open. Democrats' sweeping midterm win fuelled optimism the Iran War could end soon, sending oil lower: Brent plunged 10% below $100/bbl and the S&P 500 Energy Index fell 4.8%, its worst session since April 2025, while the S&P rose 1.6% and the VIX sat near 17. Separately, investors bet a Democratic-controlled Congress will force AI spending cuts companies have wanted, lifting Amazon and Microsoft over 6% each and the Magnificent Seven 2.2%, even as broad-based de-grossing hit the APAC AI supply chain (Kospi -6%, TAIEX -3%) after Qualcomm guided below consensus on rising costs, a read negative for handset OEMs MediaTek and AAC. China is framed as the post-midterm rotation beneficiary (HSTECH +5%, KWEB +4.5%). London's ETD desk reports broad European buying yesterday (CAC, OMX, EM futures) and a later rotation into Euro Banks funded by selling VGZ6. The day ahead: BoE decision at 12:00 (4.0% expected) and US jobless claims at 13:30 (196K expected).
